svg.text: High-Throughput LLM Serving - V1 Engine - PagedAttention + Continuous Batching - SOSP 2023
PagedAttention - fixed-size KV blocks on GPU
Block table: logical token pos - physical block
Prefix caching - chained block hash lookup
Manages worker pool - one worker per GPU
TP / PP / DP / EP distributed setup
Profiles GPU memory for KV cache capacity
Prepare input tensors - attention metadata - block tables
Model forward pass - Attention module + KV store
Sampler: greedy / temperature / beam / spec decode
CUDA graphs for decode - torch.compile integration
EngineCore step: schedule batch - dispatch executor - update request state - emit outputs
Iteration-level scheduling - requests join/leave batch every forward pass
Step 1: Client prompt arrives - tokenize - create Request with block table state
Step 2: Scheduler - schedule running + admit waiting - prefix cache hit check
Step 3: KVCacheManager.allocate_slots - block alloc or preempt on OOM
Step 4: Executor dispatches SchedulerOutput - GPUModelRunner forward + sample
Step 5: Update request state - stream tokens - free blocks on finish - repeat
Prefill phase: many tokens/seq - Decode phase: 1 token/seq - mixed in same batch
Slot freed on sequence finish immediately filled by waiting request - no padding waste
OS virtual-memory inspired KV cache - under 4% memory waste vs naive pre-allocation
Prefill node - decode node KV xfer
Up to 24x throughput vs HF Transformers - industry standard rollout engine for RL training
reset_prefix_cache on weight update (RLHF) - sleep mode frees GPU for training colocation
NVIDIA CUDA + AMD ROCm + Intel XPU + Google TPU - NGC Docker - multi-node - metrics + tracing
Init path: load ModelConfig - profile GPU mem - init KV blocks - spawn workers - warm up CUDA graphs
Step path: schedule - allocate blocks - forward - sample - update state - free/evict blocks - stream output
Sources: vllm-project/vllm - docs.vllm.ai architecture - SOSP 2023 PagedAttention paper - vLLM V1 engine design
